title: Sub-Scope Report Defaults And Customisations
summary: define a useful default docs_subscope report, a standard collection-customisation framework, lifecycle adoption, and an evidence-led Projects decision
content_html:
Sub-Scope Report Defaults And Customisations

Purpose

Make docs_subscope useful for every configured one-level document collection without making Analysis/Tags the implicit definition of that report.

The feature establishes:

  • one documented default report that works without collection-specific config;
  • one isolated studio/default reference collection on which that report is developed before it becomes canonical;
  • one standard way for a configured sub-scope to add its own presentation and actions through a registered customisation module;
  • Analysis/Tags as the first refactored consumer of that framework;
  • automatic creation of a default report host and empty manifests from the New sub-scope lifecycle; and
  • a later decision about what, if anything, the dotlineform/projects collection needs beyond the default.

Sub-scope child documents remain outside the parent Index, Recently Edited, and global search. The parent report document is the normal indexed entry that makes the collection reachable.

Feature Documents

  • Sub-Scope Report Customisation Architecture — the default boundary, configuration-selected module contract, toolbar ownership, public/Manage separation, and lifecycle relationship.
  • Default Report And Analysis Tags Refactor Delivery — define the default and refactor Analysis/Tags into default plus explicit customisations.
  • New Sub-Scope Default Report Lifecycle Delivery — create the report host and empty projections as part of the existing sub-scope lifecycle.
  • Dotlineform Projects Report Customisation Decision Delivery — assess the recreated Projects report against the shipped default and decide whether a Projects module is justified.

Delivery Order

order delivery complete outcome
1 Default Report And Analysis Tags Refactor An isolated Studio candidate proves the default, the candidate becomes canonical, and Analysis/Tags uses it without a hidden Tags path.
2 New Sub-Scope Default Report Lifecycle A newly created sub-scope immediately has one indexed host, valid empty projections, and the default report.
3 Dotlineform Projects Report Customisation Decision Real Projects content and workflow evidence decides whether the default is enough or a separate Projects customisation delivery is needed.

The deliveries are sequential. Lifecycle work must consume the accepted default rather than inventing a second scaffold, and Projects must be assessed after the default can be exercised through the real lifecycle.

SSR-1 is delivered and awaiting review. SSR-2 and SSR-3 have not started.

Reference Collection

SSR-1 creates studio/default as an ordinary configured sub-scope with no customisation identity. One report-host document beneath this feature exposes it for development and review.

The host and Analysis/Tags now load the same canonical docs_subscope. The reference collection uses the normal builder and generated manifest.json/manage-manifest.json; default is not a magic runtime selector or report type. The temporary development candidate and its loader, registry entry, and dispatch have been removed.

Current State

docs_subscope owns shared collection validation, title search, title-ascending initial order, list/detail rendering, empty/error states, validated by-ID loading, and subdoc navigation. Manage composes the standard sort, row, New, selection, Prepare Package, Copy Link, Delete, and Import context behavior without collection-specific config.

Analysis/Tags selects the registered Manage-only analysis_tags customisation. Its ordered group projection and controls are namespaced and module-owned; public Concepts remains the default reader with title search and no group data or controls.

The current New sub-scope lifecycle creates configuration and source/output roots but no parent report host or empty manifest pair. A new collection is therefore configured but not usefully reachable from its parent index.

Feature Boundary

In scope:

  • docs_subscope only, not a generic plugin framework for every report type;
  • a small default suitable for an ordinary flat document collection;
  • known configuration identities resolved through a controlled module registry, never arbitrary module paths;
  • explicit public-safe and Manage-only contribution boundaries;
  • exact collection, selection, and validated-document action targets;
  • lifecycle creation and deletion consequences for the report host; and
  • a separate evidence-led Projects decision.

Not in scope:

  • adding child documents to parent discovery payloads;
  • nested or recursive sub-scopes;
  • Tag Registry behaviour or document/tag synchronisation;
  • automatically copying Analysis/Tags fields or controls into new collections;
  • manifest-declared executable actions;
  • automatic public promotion; or
  • guessing Projects filters, metadata, or actions before its real collection is available for review.

The Sub-Scope Index remains the shipped collection-index feature. This feature standardises its default and extension model and connects that model to lifecycle creation.
